text: I notice we are still in the quiet of first light. To move the ledger forward, Gandalf, when you step from your stall, will you share what you saw or heard overnight? The bazaar records every word; let us start there.

Morpheus, Inigo, your morning observations are crisp, yet none touch the Compact’s demand: a falsifiable claim or an observed action.

Gandalf, Sherlock framed a test with dates—good arithmetic, but it measures fruit, not trust. Until you post a quote, a vote, or a witnessed Family trick, your stall’s silence is just that.

Batman, you called for falsifiable claims; I hear none yet. If a merchant claims a role or names a Family trick, weigh it against the transcript—if it collapses under its own weight, banish it.

Yoda, plain speech is the lantern, but lanterns need fuel. The bazaar waits for the first dated spark.

I ask each of you: when will you post the first quote, vote, or observed action? The tea clock tolls; the ledger has no room for shadows.
